'''Daniel Zajfman''' ({{Langx|he|דניאל זייפמן}}; born June 7, 1959) is an Israeli [[physicist]] whose main research interests are centered on the physics of simple [[molecular ion]]s. On December 1, 2006, he was elected as the tenth president of the [[Weizmann Institute]].

==Early life==
Daniel Zajfman was born in [[Brussels]], Belgium. He joined the [[Hashomer Hatzair]] movement while studying at the [[Athénée Robert Catteau]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.israelvalley.com/2017/09/06/israel-bruno-maire-rencontre-daniel-zajfman-a-linstitut-weizman/|trans-title=The words of Daniel Zajfman (Weizman Institute) to Bruno Le Maire. - IsraelValley |title=Les mots de Daniel Zajfman (Institut Weizman) à Bruno Le Maire. - IsraelValley |date=6 September 2017 |access-date=2018-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909190631/http://www.israelvalley.com/2017/09/06/israel-bruno-maire-rencontre-daniel-zajfman-a-linstitut-weizman/ |archive-date=2017-09-09 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 1979 he emigrated to Israel where he met his wife, Joëlle Hayoun. In 1983 he graduated in [[Physics]] (B.Sc.), at the [[Technion]], Israel Institute of Technology, [[Haifa]]. He continued his studies at the Technion and in 1989 received his PhD, in [[atomic physics]]. He conducted his post-doctoral at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]], [[Illinois]], United States. (1989–1991)

==Career==
In 1991 he returned to Israel and began his career as a senior scientist at the Dept. of [[Particle Physics]] ([[Weizmann Institute]] of Science). In 1997, he was appointed Associate Professor and was promoted to full professor in 2003. Since 2001, he has been an external member of the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]] in [[Heidelberg]], Germany, and in 2005, he was appointed as a Director at this [[Max Planck Institute]].

On December 1, 2006, he was elected as the tenth president of the [[Weizmann Institute]], the youngest ever. He was in turn succeeded in 2019 by [[Alon Chen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.miragenews.com/11th-president-of-weizmann-institute-and-four-new-vice-presidents-take-office/|title=11th President of Weizmann Institute and Four New Vice Presidents Take Office|date=December 1, 2019|website=Mirage News}}</ref>

On January 1, 2020, he was elected as the Chair of the Academic Board of the Israel Science Foundation.

In 2023 he received the [[Harnack Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpg.de/20492897/daniel-zajfman-harnack-medal|title=The Max Planck Society honours Daniel Zajfman with the Harnack Medal in recognition of his remarkable contributions to the advancement of science and German-Israeli cooperation|date=June 22, 2023|website=Max-planck-gesellschaft}}</ref> for his contributions to the advancement of science and German-Israeli cooperation

==Research and patents==
His research focuses on the [[reaction dynamics]] of small [[molecule]]s and how they influence the composition of the [[interstellar medium]].  He recreates the conditions of [[outer space]] in the laboratory using special devices called '[[ion trap]]s' or '[[storage ring]]s'. In these devices, he is able to briefly store and measure the properties of small amounts of material, as little as a few hundred [[atom]]s or molecules-worth, under the extreme conditions of [[Interstellar space|interstellar]] space (especially very low temperatures and low densities). Some of his research has focused on the puzzle of how complex molecules are formed in outer space.
